answers.explanation: Viruses are considered living because they possess transmittable characters, which they pass on to their offspring.
Amoeba and Paramecium both have a contractile vacuole for removing excess water.
Hydra takes in food through its mouth and egests undigested material back through the mouth.
Coelenterates such as Hydra reproduce by budding.
Algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes all need water for fertilisation, since their male gametes swim.
Fern spores are light and are dispersed mainly by the wind.
In bryophytes the sex organs are produced on the gametophyte generation.
Lizards have homodont teeth, which are all of similar shape.
External fertilisation takes place in toads, where eggs and sperm meet in water.
The suckers of the tapeworm scolex hold it fast to the intestinal wall of the host.
Light bones reduce body weight, which adapts birds to flight.
Nephridia are the excretory organs of the earthworm.
Yellow fever is spread by mosquitoes, not by housefly.
Sieve tubes are thin-walled and remain living at maturity.
Saprophytes digest their food outside their bodies, which is extracellular digestion.
The first step in photosynthesis is the activation of chlorophyll by light.
Glucose is a reducing sugar and gives a brick-red precipitate with Benedict's solution.
The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes and the hormone insulin.
Villi increase the surface area of the small intestine for absorption of digested food.
The xylem is still intact after the removal of bark and phloem, so mineral salts still move up the stem.
Transpiration is measured with a potometer.
Anthocyanins are the pigments responsible for red, purple and blue flower colours.
Etiolation is the development of pale, weak plants grown in the absence of light.
Tendons attach muscles indirectly to bones.
Oestrogen and progesterone are produced in large amounts by the placenta during pregnancy.
Parthenocarpic fruits develop without fertilisation and are usually seedless.
Elephant grass is propagated vegetatively by suckers.
The semicircular canals of the inner ear are concerned with balance.
Gametes carry half the diploid number, so 16 divided by 2 gives 8 chromosomes.
All F1 flies are normal-winged because the normal wing is dominant, and three-quarters of F2 are normal-winged.
People in blood group AB have no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in their serum, so they can receive any blood group.
Haemophilia results from a mutation of genes that control the blood clotting mechanism.
Water, temperature and soil are the abiotic factors of the savanna ecosystem.
A mouse eats both plant and animal food, so it is an omnivore.
The hawk is at the top of the food chain, so it has the lowest population.
The salinity of brackish water increases during the dry season, when less fresh water flows in.
Aestivation is the physiological adaptation of animals that survive dry conditions by becoming dormant.
Malaria, cholera and river blindness are spread mainly by insect vectors or water-based vectors such as mosquitoes and blackflies.
Refuse burnt in an incinerator releases smoke and gases that pollute the air.
Bacteria in root nodules receive protection and carbohydrates from the host plant.
Denitrifying bacteria release free nitrogen into the atmosphere.
